members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Identify each reaction and product containing the indicated element. Determine hybridization of the element in the product. sp³d² hybridization corresponds to coordination number 6 (octahedral) with d orbitals involved, typical for hypervalent or transition metal complexes with 6 ligands. Evaluate each:
(i) Na4XeO6 + conc H2SO4 cold → likely XeO3 or XeO4? Cold conc H2SO4 with Na4XeO6 probably yields XeO3 (Xe in +4) or XeF? No F. XeO3 is trigonal pyramidal (sp3 hybridized). No d involvement. So not sp3d2.
(ii) Br2 + excess F2 → likely BrF5 or BrF3? Excess F2 gives BrF5 (Br +5) with coordination 5, not 6. Could be BrF? Not sp3d2.
(iii) CoCl2, NH4Cl, excess NH3, air excluded → likely formation of [Co(NH3)6]2+ complex (Co(II) octahedral). Co2+ with 6 NH3 gives sp3d2 hybridization. So yes.
(iv) Ni + CO, 50–60°C → likely Ni(CO)4 (tetrahedral Ni(0) with 4 CO ligands). Tetrahedral uses sp3 hybridization, not sp3d2.
(v) NO3- + Zn or Al, conc NaOH warm → likely formation of nitrite or ammonia? Reaction of nitrate with metal in basic warm gives NO or N2? Typically Zn + NaOH + NO3- gives Zn(OH)2 and NO? Might produce N2O or N2? Not sp3d2.
Thus only reaction (iii) yields sp3d2 hybridized Co. So total number of reactions where indicated element in its product is sp3d2 hybridised = 1.
But check if any other could be sp3d2: Br2 + excess F2 could give BrF6-? Not typical. Co complex is most plausible.
Thus answer integer 1.

members.working:
Analyse each product:
(i) Na₄XeO₆ + conc. cold H₂SO₄ → XeO₄ (xenon tetroxide, tetrahedral, sp³). Not sp³d².
(ii) Br₂ + excess F₂ → BrF₅ (bromine pentafluoride, square pyramidal, sp³d² hybridisation with one lone pair). sp³d² ✓
(iii) CoCl₂ + NH₄Cl + NH₃ (air excluded) → [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₂; Co(II) d⁷, complex is high spin (Co(II) weak field), octahedral geometry—hybridisation sp³d² (outer orbital). sp³d² ✓
(iv) Ni + CO at 50–60 °C → Ni(CO)₄ (Mond process), tetrahedral, sp³. Not sp³d².
(v) NO₃⁻ + Zn/Al + NaOH → NH₃ (or hydroxylamine); N in NH₃ is sp³. Not sp³d².
So only reactions (ii) BrF₅ and (iii) [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺ have the element sp³d² hybridised. Total = 2.
members.reasoning:
Let's analyze each reaction.

(i) Na₄XeO₆ + cold conc. H₂SO₄ → XeO₄ (xenon tetroxide). Xe in XeO₄: tetrahedral, sp³ hybridised. Not sp³d².

(ii) Br₂ + excess F₂ → BrF₅ (with excess F₂, bromine forms BrF₅; BrF₇ doesn't exist). BrF₅: square pyramidal, sp³d². Yes.

(iii) CoCl₂ + NH₄Cl + excess NH₃, air excluded → [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₂ (Co²⁺, hexaamminecobalt(II)). Co²⁺ d⁷. [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺ is high spin? Actually Co(II) ammine is high spin d⁷, octahedral, uses sp³d² outer orbital hybridisation. Yes, sp³d² (outer orbital complex). So counts.

(iv) Ni + CO, 50-60°C → Ni(CO)₄. Ni: sp³ hybridised, tetrahedral. Not sp³d².

(v) NO₃⁻ + Zn/Al + conc. NaOH, warm → NH₃ (reduction of nitrate to ammonia in alkaline medium). N in NH₃: sp³. Not sp³d².

So count = 2 (BrF₅ and [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺).

Wait, check (iii): with air excluded, Co²⁺ remains; product [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₂. Co²⁺ d⁷ high spin octahedral → sp³d². Yes.

Answer: 2.
